x: This no doubt kept many spectators away and may also have affected the number of starters, although I hope that our members cannot be accused of being fair-weather athletes! In the 100 yards senior race we saw Denis Merrett beat Basil Walden by inches with our new member, I.

This was our last “ home ” meeting of the track season, and we had senior and junior matches against our old friends in the light-blue vests. In the senior events we saw I. Mayers, our coloured sprinter, win the 100 yards in 10.4 secs., and he was also second to A.
In the 100 yards I Mayers was 2nd and R.

Those who turned up certainly gave of their best but there is no doubt we should have done much better had we been properly represented. Ron Holtum was 4th in 100 yards and I. Mayers 3rd in the 220, whilst in the 440 yards our two runners were 5th and 6th.
Porter throwing the hammer for Essex was unplaced but gained standard. On the track Dave Merret (Surrey) and I. Mayers (Middlesex) reached the final of the 220 yards but were unplaced.

Records galore is, I think, an apt description for the Bel's efforts in the Beverley Baxter Trophy Meeting at Southgate on July 2nd, for track and meeting records were broken in no less than seven events. I.
1st N.Caves 44'9". 2nd C.Jones 43'10½". 3rd I.Mayers 43'8" The 3 miles, with a field of 25, proved that we could really start putting teams in 2 mile races, for some excellent times were recorded.
100 yards · I.Mayers / J.Vivian · May 1955 / Aug.1965 · 9.9 secs.
